The HATNet planetary transit survey continues to discover new planetary candidates which are subsequently verified by other teams using telescopes of varying sizes. Although the HATNet collaboration has identified significant trends regarding the distribution of planets based on mass ratio, their initial findings were limited to specific systems detected by other detectors. By analyzing their own data, it has been possible to uncover a broader pattern encompassing a broad spectrum of planetary masses. Our research specifically focuses on validating 1100 robustly confirmed planetary candidates discovered by the HATNet collaboration within the context of the broader distribution of planets based on mass ratio. By comparing and combining our own research with previously published studies, it has been demonstrated that the distribution of planets found by the HATNet collaboration generally aligns with the overall planetary trend, yet distinct differences emerge when examining specific mass ranges. The discrepancies observed within the HATNet data could be attributed to a few potential causes including: selection biases stemming from the HATNet telescope's wide-field observation, variations in the density of planetary systems between nearby and more distant exoplanet host stars, as well as possible discrepancies in the distribution of planets across different wavelength ranges.

High-resolution global illumination image generation is achieved with remarkable speed and efficiency through a novel light transport representation known as VD-slab tracing, which breaks down the rendering process into discrete 3D volumes containing pre-computed radiance and importance information. This representation can be reconstructed from the popular Bidirectional Importance Sampling method using Latin rotation point sets to optimize storage. To compute shadows, an innovative slab-based approach estimates the importance and accumulates importance based on contributions from nearby adjacent slabs, thereby reducing memory requirements by a significant factor of approximately 100 when compared to full volume storage. To achieve stunning visual results, high importance is maintained through a convolution operation applied to Importance Accumulation to preserve fine details. This approach enables photorealistic image generation at resolutions up to 4096^2 within a remarkable timeframe of under 30 seconds on a single GPU.

The development of multi-stream probabilistic O-D models based on Bayesian inference and Gibbs sampling has allowed for precise traffic delay estimation and finite set parameter characterization.  However, conventional Monte Carlo simulations used for parameter estimation often suffer from excessive computation time and inaccurate results due to the high dimensionality of likelihood functions.  Using the properties of Gibbs sampling, this research proposes a new estimation approach that applies Lasso regularization for covariance matrix estimation and non-linear regression for mean vector estimation within likelihood optimization.  By utilizing Lasso regularization for covariance matrix estimation and non-linear regression for mean vector estimation, this approach significantly reduces the complexity of Monte Carlo simulations, as evidenced by a case study showing reductions of 4 orders of magnitude for one stream and 2 orders of magnitude for another.  Furthermore, application of this approach results in the optimal estimation of distribution parameters for each travel time stream and aligns estimated distribution means with the median of unregularized posterior samples.  Consequently, this research ap- plicably demonstrates the efficacy of Lasso and nonlinear regression regression in improving Bayesian O-D demand modeling and accelerating Monte Carlo simulations by several orders of magnitude.

This article investigates how weak nonlinear frequency dispersion and coupling nonlinearity affect a network of phase-locked oscillators with variable frequencies. The first part explores the stability of synchronized states under various dispersions, while the second examines both stability and performance metric - lock range - across different network topologies, including random small-world configurations.

Two prominent algorithms exist for creating a random, spanning tree that covers all vertices of a given graph uniformly, known as Wilson's and Prim's algorithms. Wilson's algorithm excels on sparse graphs, particularly those with a large number of edges relative to vertices, but straggles on dense graphs. In contrast, Prim's algorithm, which often requires $O(m \log n)$ time, performs well on dense graphs. In contrast, we introduce a clever combination of these algorithms that excels at generating a uniform spanning tree within $\O(\sqrt{n}\log^3 n)$ time, significantly improving upon Wilson's performance on dense graphs. Moreover, our enhanced approach can be integrated into Bataglier's algorithm for generating a uniform spanning forest, matching its best possible runtime of $\O(\min\{\sqrt{n}, k\log^{2+\eps} (k/n)\} )$. Lastly, our method offers a novel perspective on tree-building processes, providing a new proof that validates a claim made by Benczúr and Sudán.

Our proposed dataset, MusicTM-Dataset, aims to bridge the gap in research by providing a comprehensive framework for research in self-supervised multimodal representation learning. As numerous music information extraction techniques already exist, our focus lies in developing a robust musical representation that can effectively capture intricate relationships between music and external cues such as audio, visual, textual, and metadata information. To validate our approach and share our findings, we have established a comprehensive music representation learning framework and an extensive dataset that includes 116,911 text descriptions, 14,531,151 metadata tags, 2,580,465 video videos, and 12,842,012 music-video pairs. Through this framework, researchers can explore cross-modal learning, data aggregation, self-supervised learning, and data augmentation tasks, while also conducting comprehensive performance evaluations and visualizing results via multidimensional scaling, nearest neighbor analysis, and linear probing.

We introduce Ontodia, a visual exploration tool for datasets like Wikidata that enhances user understanding of data structure. Currently, explorations of Wikidata are limited to static visualizations, which don't provide interactivity. Ontodia addresses this by enabling users to navigate large datasets, interactively query data, and dynamically generate visualizations. One Ontodia instance focuses on Wikidata, making it accessible to any user of the platform. Wikidata contains vast amounts of information, with entries linked to databases like MySQL and MongoDB. Our tool showcases exploration of 15 data tables, allowing users to understand their data structure, formulate queries, and generate visualizations (e.g., world maps, timelines, and word clouds).

In a trapped one-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensate, traveling dark solitons, which move at non-relativistic speeds, exhibit an intriguing property: they are orbital stable within this speed range, yet become orbital unstable beyond a certain threshold.

The lotse-python package, or Lotse library for short, is an open-source, cross-platform tool written in Python designed to model galaxy evolution over extensive timeframes spanning from initial collapse to the present day. Lotse facilitates the development of comprehensive galaxy evolution models over extensive cosmic timescales by offering a wide array of guidance strategies that automatically select the most suitable galaxy evolution model characteristics based on the existing properties of a galaxy and its surroundings. With its extensive functionality, Lotse enables users to implement versatile galaxy evolution models while maintaining computational efficiency. This document serves as a user's guide to using Lotse effectively, describing its core features, step-by-step implementation of guidance strategies and modeling workflows, and providing a reference to Lotse's comprehensive documentation.

Achieving a stable, high-beta nested flux surface configuration in the FRC requires careful management of transport and control of deformations. To investigate the effect of control coils on flux surface flexibility, we conducted 2D resistive MHD simulations using four coil placements. The study reveals that control coils surrounding the flux surfaces provide the optimal balance between flexibility and maintainability of nested flux surfaces. Control coils positioned inside the flux surfaces also contribute effectively to stability, albeit with the need for more particles to maintain flux-ratio integrity. The position of control coils plays a crucial role in minimizing the volume required for active feedback stabilization of flux surfaces.

A novel temperature-proton frequency shift relationship is proposed for use in temperature profiling within reactors using magnetic resonance imaging, ultimately facilitating the determination of temperature coefficients in industrial reactors. A mathematical model for this frequency shift as a function of temperature has been developed, showing its potential application when combined with the existing temperature-dependent relaxation time T2. Using this shift and relaxation time, the temperature can be calculated through the solution of a proton spin equation that incorporates temperature diffusion. Simulation results demonstrate that this proposed method can accurately calculate temperature distributions, potentially improving the accuracy of reactors' temperature measurements when used in conjunction with the T2-based temperature determination.

While experimental focus has been on creating two-species condensates, the possibility exists for their numbers to be unlimited. A theoretical exploration using the Gross-Pitaevskii equation indicates that, when multiple species are involved, the more complex the mixture, the greater the likelihood of forming distinct condensates.

Solar flares release energy at unprecedented rates, exceeding all known mechanical explosions in the universe. To comprehend this phenomenon, researchers examine rapid magnetic transformations, specifically the swift movement of solar flares' induced transients. These transants move at significant speeds, ranging from 500 meters per second to over 1000 kilometers per second, significantly exceeding the typical solar plasma flow rate of around 100 meters per second. By utilizing solar image data from the DSTA repository, researchers analyzed three instances of magnetic transient behavior associated with the X2.2 class solar flare on June 5th, 2014, observing their trajectories and speeds across sunspots W26 and W27, respectively, between 12:25:00 UTC and 13:00:00 UTC, observed by the SDO AIA telescope at various speeds and distances, respectively, observing magnetic transients moving along a connecting line or separate paths, respectively, observing magnetic transients moving at varying speeds or stopping temporarily.

Our demonstration of the Madsen-Weiss theorem relies on the $b$-principle and two stability theorems. One stability result is novel, whereas the other aligns with existing results from Independence Day theorems. All mentioned principles are specific instances of general phenomena derived from novel principles and theorems presented in this paper. These concepts are developed using only oriented cobordism, constituting a $b$-theory. Additionally, this approach yields a novel proof independence of Stable Boardard Theory.

This paper develops novel, data-independent BDDC templates and analyzes their effectiveness when paired with different finite element discretizations. By establishing precise bounds, we prove that the BDDC preconditioner achieves optimal performance relative to the subdomain sizes, and identify the BDDC components responsible for achieving this optimal scaling. These results enable us to construct adaptive BDDC algorithms optimal in two adaptive adaptive settings: when edges are refined and when vertices are refined.

I investigated Wikipedia's tagging systems, examining their evolution, functions, and users' labeling patterns from 2008 to 2020. By doing so, I aimed to grasp how volunteers interact with these tags, which shed light on general tagging system dynamics. My analysis revealed significant insights into how dynamic tags, initially created for2020I1 editing efficiency, grew in number and established a supply chain, where tags new editors adopted were often selected from experienced editors. However, this insight led to unresolved issues, such as duplicated tags and evolving meanings. In contrast, management tags, which were used for community-led editorial work, were rarely labeled by others, which highlighted how existing content was divided into distinct editorial segments. These findings, though specific to Wikipedia, have broader implications, illustrating how tagging systems support broader collaborative efforts and enhance our understanding of unlabeled systems. Ultimately, these insights inform the design of more effective tagging systems, especially in areas like AI assistance, safety filters, guidance, and management, where mechanisms can be improved based on actual labeling behavior.

Acoustic metamaterials, particularly those made of microstructures, are designed to manipulate sound waves in precise ways. However, understanding the behavior of tiny structures requires considering additional physical effects like temperature and fluid dynamics, which can have a significant impact on their performance. We examine the thermal-viscous response in common microstructures used in acoustic metamaterials, including flexible membranes, rigid scatterers, and narrow channels. Our analysis indicates that the temperature and pressure oscillations obey the same equations as in large-scale systems, but the acoustic variables follow different equations, which means the thermal-viscous effect varies among different microstructures. Furthermore, we observe that the thermal-viscous effect becomes more significant at higher frequencies of sound, which means it cannot be ignored in the design of acoustic metamaterials.

This research examines the low-frequency behavior of the solutions to the one-dimensional FENE dumbbell model with a nonlinear elastic force. Within specific initial conditions and time frames, we identify a space transformation that maintains solution structure. Consequently, we demonstrate that the solutions satisfy certain inequalities in terms of Besov spaces. Our analysis extends to a wider range of $L^p$-based Besov spaces than previously possible. Moreover, by applying a unique space framework, we establish that the global solutions belong to a finite-dimensional Besov space after some time has passed. Our theory includes a specific parameter special function and provides a parameter-dependent bound for the norm of the solutions. Our results complement the work of a UMD frame by showing that the solutions have only a limited number of long-term characteristics.

Myriad small-scale base stations can be utilized to serve users moving in clusters by incorporating mobile integrated access and backhaul techniques at lower frequency spectrum usage. Since the rate at which these stations can communicate through backhaul is influenced by their proximity and orientation to each other, the potential network size and the movement patterns of these stations significantly impact how they provide connectivity to mobile users. To address these considerations, we introduce a method that selects a maximum number of these stations, their network connections, and their backhaul communications to maximize the service they provide while considering their movement patterns and random orientations. By forming a network on the fly through the selection of these stations, their shared connections, and their backhaul, we provide service to mobile users in the most efficient way possible. To solve the resulting optimization challenge, we convert it into an integer programming problem whose parameters depend on the station positions, which are determined using selected factors including the distribution of their backhaul communications. By taking into account the distribution of these factors, we are able to design a stochastic integer programming model whose complexity is easier to manage and whose solution is closer to the optimal result. Through numerical simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in selecting a network, backhaul, and orientation of these stations to maximize the service provided to mobile users in the group.

The performance of the alternative controlled variable (ACV) stability algorithm heavily relies on an accurate estimation of its key components, particularly the covariance matrix of the error term, which is often estimated using parameters that require tuning. In this study, an examination of the influence of these tuning parameters on the covariance matrix's conventional inverse maximum likelihood (AMIL) and generalized AMIL estimators is conducted, with implications for the stability algorithm's overall performance. An analysis of the estimators' behavior across various parameters, including their interdependence, computational demands, and sensitivity, is carried out within the framework of the stability algorithm. Two approaches to component optimization are compared, with considerations for their impact on ACV stability and overall algorithm efficiency.

In this project, we trace the quantization of energy levels in an electromagnetic field, closely following Greiner and Müller's "Relativistic Quantum Mechanics" and "Relativistic Quantum Mechanics. Non-Abelian Fields." The books' introductions of the Dirac equation, specifically focusing on hydrogen bound states, led us to ask: how does allowing relative motion between the electron and proton impact the system? We utilize the reduced mass to calculate the Balmer series hydrogen spectral lines for both non-relativistic and relativistic scenarios.

The recent surge in reinforcement learning success can be attributed to massive tool collections leveraging high-performance GPU clusters. However, many of these collections have complex tool and curriculum designs that render algorithm comparisons challenging. In this study, we streamline existing reinforcement learning collections, implementing only controlled changes to curriculum and tool controls while maintaining legal experimentation space. Using our simplified framework, we identify simple, effective collections of hyperparameters, tools, and courses. This paper presents our methodology for constructing efficient collections, develops our controller system, and validates our approach through four case studies showcasing its effectiveness in hyperparameter optimization and transparent analysis of existing collections. Our open-source repository enables others to contribute and customize our controller, which we employ to reproduce previous studies and conduct new research.

Liger is a scalable framework for loading, processing, and serving datasets in large-scale machine learning operations, incorporated into LinkedIn's recommendation service. The user defines a data interface describing the data's structure, enabling the automatic generation of efficient serving code through its processing in a Python-based data serving environment. A data interface representation and implementation details will be presented, along with the architecture and benefits of Liger, supplemented by performance evaluation through benchmark studies comparing it to custom data serving pipelines and other popular libraries.

Building upon existing research, we investigate traveling wave solutions near the Couette flow with a small velocity difference between the plates, particularly for periodic domains. Under the assumption of a sufficient smoothness level, our results indicate that, given any non-zero wave profile that is more than 10 steps smoother than the Couette flow, there exists a corresponding non-trivial traveling wave solution within a small neighborhood of the flow. This finding highlights the necessity of non-resonance conditions, as well as suggests the potential for required regularity levels to be potentially lower.

Our method controls polarization deterministically using a single streak camera and a machine learning algorithm. This efficient approach can be utilized in various applications such as polarization analysis, monitoring in spintronics and non-linear optics, and more. We trained a random forest classifier with 500 trees using 5000 synthetic data points and successfully classified the polarization with up to 85% accuracy and extend dynamic range of 0.84 log units (from 0.15 to 23). Furthermore, our technique might offer an economically viable solution for polarimetry where high precision is not essential but a broad polarization range and precision are crucial.

This paper extends the results of Liang and Zhang's study on a discrete Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equation from [20], which examined a model incorporating periodic noise driving a particle's motion in one dimension. Specifically, it investigates the existence of a kinetic equation that can be derived from this discrete model. Our findings reveal that the parameter $\lambda$, which controls the amplitude of the periodic noise, significantly impacts solution existence. Moreover, we demonstrate solution non-existence for certain values of $\lambda$ below a particular threshold and establish a continuous family of solutions for all such $\lambda$ in this range. Furthermore, we show that the solution set exhibits continuity with respect to $\lambda$ and characterize the behavior of solutions as $\lambda$ approaches this critical value from below.

South Africa's COVID-19 responses were influenced by official data, which had data quality issues due to inaccuracies, inconsistencies, and difficulties in access.  In order to address these challenges, a data quality assessment was conducted on key COVID-19 data sources, which were of concern to South Africa's Data Trust.  Researchers analyzed changes in confidence intervals and investigated data discrepancies with neighboring countries to identify potential data issues.  In order to improve data analysis, an accurate data representation was developed to calculate confusion matrix metrics and identify patterns in data fluctuations.  This study provides a framework for analyzing and understanding data reliability, which may be extended for use with other single data points.  Limitations in this analysis were due to unutilized error bounds in statistics provided.  In order to address these issues, recommendations were provided for data users.

Allowing a limited number of components in a subset of integers significantly alters its behavior. For subsets $A$ of integers from $\{1,\ldots, N\}$ with a high level of additivity, where it holds that $|A+A|\leq (1+\varepsilon)N$, we explore how summing with other subsets influences the presence of arithmetic progressions. Specifically, when adding a finite number of elements from another subset $B$, given a sufficiently large $b$, we prove that the sumset $(A+b_1+\ldots+b_r+B)$ contains arithmetic progressions of any desired length $l$. Notably, if we restrict additions and let $B$ consist of multiples of a large value, our findings provide a novel method to demonstrate the presence of arithmetic progressions in certain subsets of integers, where the required length grows faster than any polynomial in $N$.

While combining multiple images or views is a common technique for improving performance, its application to video is complicated by the need to efficiently process vast amounts of data. Research has shown that hierarchical fusion methods, such as those used in multi-view video prediction, outperform single-view videos in quality, but they are limited by their inability to directly compare information from multiple views. In this paper, we introduce a new hierarchical fusion approach, ValidView, which innovates in two key areas: a validity check mechanism to integrate relevant details from multiple views, and a compact encoding method for multiple views that minimizes information loss. ValidView's novel encoding scheme, called ValidViewEncoding, identifies view pairs with high information exchange and only encodes view info for those pairs. ValidView is evaluated on several benchmarks, including multi-view video prediction and video object tracking, and outperforms state-of-the-art techniques by a significant margin.

The COVID-19 pandemic has brought immense challenges to the global community, with the SARS-CoV-2 virus spreading uncontrollably and causing a massive loss of life. The disease's spread has strained healthcare facilities, necessitating the identification of patients at high risk of requiring intensive care. This research aims to identify factors that could aid in predicting ICU admission, incorporating an exploration of feature importance, linear drift detection, and resource allocation considerations. We incorporate clinical data and demographic/clinical information extracted from insurance claims, applying a random forest model to predict ICU admission and calculating importance using the Gini index. The model's performance is assessed through Area Under the Curve (AUC) and exploration of interactions using Interaction Dominance Index (IDI), followed by a analysis of feature drift using Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) and Kolmogorov-Smirnov Enthalpy (KSE) metrics. These efforts are in line with healthcare goals of optimizing ICU resource allocation and mitigating mortality risk.

We investigate the transmission eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet boundary value problem associated with a variable speed wave equation in N-dimensional space. In a N-dimensional space, the transmission eigenvalue problem involves finding the solution u to the equation (a0^2|grad|^2 + d0^2/dt^2)u = P(x, D)u, given the nonlinear operator P, with the constraint that the integral of the squared magnitude of u over the space minus the ball, outside of the ball B, equals zero. Given the initial conditions and parameters that vary with position, our objective is to understand the behavior of the transmission eigenfunctions, particularly in relation to the exponents in the growth of these parameters, as the transmission eigenvalues approach infinity. Under the assumption of the parameters θ and β being constant, our results show the transmission eigenfunctions will concentrate around the boundary of the ball in N-dimensional space, and the integral of the squared magnitude of u, within the ball, converges to the solution of a transmission eigenvalue problem for the Laplace operator, in (N-1)-dimensional space, given the Dirichlet boundary condition on this boundary, and involves terms of the parameters θ and β and the curvature of the boundary, and involves terms of the principal curvatures of the level sets of the distance function.

This paper introduces pre-trained utterance embeddings, derived from a large corpus of user/agent dialogues, that are learned through semantic and temporal tasks. The study reveals that multi-task pre-training significantly enhances the quality of the produced representations by leveraging typical user and agent dialogue patterns. Furthermore, the proposed method shows substantial improvement in both NLU tasks from the State-of-the-art baseline across multiple benchmarks, with a particularly notable success in dialogue generation and response prediction tasks. Notably, the proposed method successfully captures the linguistic and semantic elements required for these tasks. The efficiency of the approach is also highlighted with dialogue generation results achieved using as few as 64 dimensional embeddings. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/hoosier-ai-lab/ai-dialogue.

The universal bundle functor, known as $T$, plays a crucial role in categorial topology, particularly within the category of base-pointed simplicial groups and functors that preserve products. It's essential to understand that $T$ gives rise to a specific monad structure, distinct from another $T$ defined on the category of simplicial groups, to which a different, hypermonad, is associated. Furthermore, this distinct $T$ (the monad) works cohomologically with a specific, representable, cohomology theory possessing a unique summation structure. This type of cohomology helps to understand and express a generalised, total cohomology for the fibre of a pull-back square, ultimately leading to the establishment of a corresponding spectral sequence in generalised cohomology. This spectral sequence provides a quick and direct proof for a well-known result in (total) cohomology: the Serre-Serre spectral sequence for a fibration with a base-pointed fibre. This new approach replaces a former construction relying on cohomology theory axioms, fibres in categories of spaces and groups, and a double complex.

For any finite group G, let's denoted by H(x) the count of its subgroups of order x. Our findings demonstrate that for a sufficiently large |G|, the count of its subgroups of order 2^k, for any non-negative integer k, is proportional to log_x(|G|)^k. Notably, our research also yields an innovative new proof for a conjecture made by Palfy and Palfy, which establishes that the total number of a finite group's subgroups is proportional to its square root of the group's order.

We examine various first-order variables derived from a one-dimensional, compressible flow model within a compress-rarefaction cell of the compress-N scheme. Upon applying the continuum framework, the $S^{(1,0)}$ variable leads to the Korteweg-de Vries equation, characterizing a third-order dispersive behavior. The $S^{(2,0)}$ and $S^{(1,1)}$ variables result in the Euler equations, demonstrating non-linear advection with a vanishing viscosity when a small parameter $\epsilon$ is present. The aim of study is to investigate the dispersive effects of the compress-N scheme, particularly in in-out flow conditions where oscillations may occur, by incorporating the dispersive properties of its third-order reconstruction and verifying the model through various test cases.

Visual Relationship Detection in computer vision faces challenges due to the scarcity of training data and the difficulty in capturing complex object interactions. Current approaches, which rely heavily on manually created training data, often lead to incomplete models from noisy labels. Therefore, we propose a weak-to-strong learning framework, which optimizes detection and recognition tasks simultaneously. To enhance optimization efficiency, we developed Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling, a technique that focuses on improving relationships detection using the most challenging sampled objects. Additionally, we created a novel, multi-phase data annotation process, allowing us to minimize the required training data while we refine the model. Our method yields significant performance gains over strong baseline models, with substantial improvements using zero-shot settings and a complete removal of human annotation costs. Notably, our approach achieves record-breaking performance at the AIPR task at the AI@MVLAN 2021 challenge. The proposed method will be accessible on our GitHub repository for the code and the dataset will be accessible on the Visualized-AI Relationship Dataset website.

A common issue with open quantum systems is that interactions with their environment lead to quantization loss within them. We have found, however, that the less-than-maximal entanglement acquired through weak measurement can be retrieved, and this allows for one party to give another almost any level of quantization, even in complex multi-party states. We also reveal that this method of extracting potential holds wide range of applications, allowing one party to regulate another's quantum properties. Our findings show the capacity of quantum control in an open quantum system and provide valuable insight for future uses in quantum information processing.

Social interactions have been used for self-improvement and learning from a young age. As a particular case, social network analysis uses graphs to model interpersonal relationships, where nodes represent individuals and edges represent interactions. By analyzing connections, researchers have successfully predicted individual characteristics and network structures. However, individual decisions are influenced by a complex web of connections, making it essential to personalize information spread patterns and update individual attributes over time as new interactions occur. While existing methods focus on individual nodes or simple relationships, this work addresses the need to personalize a complex, dynamic graph and updates neighborhood properties based on interactions. To this end, a novel gate mechanism is proposed, allowing the graph to select relevant information from nodes and update its structure dynamically. Through experiments on node classification and attribute prediction, this work demonstrates a model's effectiveness in leveraging GRU-based networks to update social connections and graph structure, which has significant real-world implications for embedded social networks and knowledge graphs.

In neural network training, message passing between graph nodes involves significant computational costs.  A more efficient approach, called adaptive graph sampling, focuses on selecting a smaller subset of valuable nodes to send messages to.  Currently, however, graph neighbors are chosen randomly or based on degrees, which often fails to pinpoint the nodes most crucial to the overall learning process.  A new method proposes utilizing a neural network to identify relevant nodes by minimizing the overall network's loss.  By sampling only these selected neighbors, the method reduces the computational complexity without compromising performance.  Also introduced is a technique for adaptive message aggregation that selects features from neighbors' messages to reduce complexity.  A thorough evaluation using classification and link prediction tasks across diverse datasets reveals that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches while minimizing computational costs.

This proposal outlines an implementation strategy for Multiple Constant Multiplication using a linear feedback shift register and binary point arithmetic, building on a previous work. It suggests adding rules for error propagation to guide the integration of inexact results, which can enhance performance, shorten latency, and reduce power consumption.

Recent breakthroughs in quantum computing have sparked significant interest in quantum deep learning, with numerous studies exploring this breakthrough technology. As various frameworks for quantum computing and deep learning emerge, a thorough review of the latest findings in quantum deep learning has become necessary. This study aims to offer a comprehensive overview of quantum deep learning's underlying principles, key concepts, and applications, focusing on the latest advancements. Furthermore, open challenges and potential future research directions in quantum deep learning are discussed.

The RF technology originally designed for high energy physics is proving equally valuable in various other accelerators, such as those used in therapy, cargo inspection, security, and even radar and communication systems, the latter powered by klystrons. This comprehensive guide provides an accessible entry point to the principles of RF technology, emphasizing the concept of a cavity, while providing an exhaustive reference in the appendices for engineers and physicists with advanced knowledge of the subject, covering topics like klystrons, travel-wave tubes, amplifiers, switches, generators, and power handling and line components.

The muon g-2 experiment's results have sparked intense interest in the potential of a high-energy muon collider, with 3, 30, and 100 TeV data sets set to offer groundbreaking insights into specific new physics models and broaden their excluded parameter space. However, several technical hurdles are inherent in the design, construction, and operation of a muon collider: accurate muon detection necessitates dense sensing that inevitably interferes with its otherwise straightforward detection, while additionally causing significant energy loss and challenging head-on particle beam integration. Research focuses heavily on novel sensing technologies such as TTarget detectors and the GEM-based EM-Calendar detector system, with integration into the 30 TeV collider's detector design already being thoroughly explored. Furthermore, the collider's cooling system is another area of technical innovation, with a 300 K normal-conducting superconductor alternative thoroughly examined for its ability to mitigate the impact of the heat generated by its high-radiation environment on its cooling requirements.

We examine how a relativistic fluid with viscosity and small perturbations evolves over time in one particular theory, which is also characterized by some degree of randomness. In this framework, we derive the relativistic generalized Navier-Stokes equations, which incorporate the effects of pressure, viscosity, and randomness into our analysis. We then obtain the dispersion relations for these perturbations, which describe their evolution over time, and compare them to the relations predicted by the Fokker-Planck and Langevin approaches, as well as the results from recent non-equilibrium field theory and effective kinetic theory. We find that the three methods yield remarkably similar fluid dynamics behavior within a certain range of conditions, but start to diverge outside of this range, where the non-equilibrium field theory's results suggest a greater degree of randomness than predicted by the Fokker-Planck and Langevin approaches.

The calculation of particle radiation from massive black holes formed at a black hole formation density threshold in dark matter structures has been performed. Researchers used the relationship between a dark matter halo's peak scale and its peak epoch, as well as the dark matter distribution function in an expanding Euclidean space. In this type of space, the flux from Hawking radiation decreases with time. For black holes within certain mass ranges, the initial intense radiation may not outshine the background radiation in certain energy ranges, due to limitations imposed by dark matter halo's energy density. However, if dark matter consists of primordial black holes, they could potentially outshine the radiation from Hawking radiation from scalar black holes. For black holes with masses less than or equal to $10^{12}$ kg, this effect is most pronounced.

This circuit evaluation architecture is built upon the Satisfiability Problem, using a sequential circuit and a set of inputs to determine its output value, which is calculated through a specific order and input assignment. We have designed a circuit-based model, based on a C++ program, and compared its complexity to the original program. By analyzing circuit parameters such as the number of outputs, inputs, and gates, and comparing them to program variables like function calls, assignments, and operations, we found that our proposed method effectively maps the original code to the circuit. This approach was validated through performance tests of a customized pipelined CPU, which added control for negative cycling and was optimized with parallel processing capabilities, and achieved significant speedup over the original circuit evaluation.

This paper reveals two major breakthrough achievements in Valued CSPs. Firstly, it's the first instance where a PTAS is demonstrated for a class of valued CSPs. We found that a minimum strong valued constraint algebra allows for efficient valuation of crisp constraints and quasi-single valued constraints, yielding a PTAS for such minimisation problems. Secondly, it's been proven that every valued CSP based on a strong valued constraint algebra has a constant-factor approximation algorithm solve, extending previous results for specific algebras. These new findings are achieved through innovative techniques, including a novel canonical algebra concept and reduction from valued cliques to valued independent sets in specific graph classes.

Recent studies on few-shot parsing demonstrate the potential of using limited training data (a small number of trees) to improve parsing performance on new datasets. Notably, these methods excel especially when new datasets have a smaller number of annotated trees. Our analysis reveals, however, that these methods are not always optimal when a substantial number of training instances (a larger number of trees) are present in a target dataset. In such scenarios, their performance may start to lag behind that of baseline parsers. In this investigation, we introduce FPIO, a novel few-shot parsing method grounded on the principles of few-shot learning. Unlike previous approaches that train entire networks specific to the target dataset, FPIO introduces a single, shared neural network parameterized in advance. This shared network maintains consistent special skills across multiple target datasets while enhancing its expertise over time through continual learning. This shared network serves two critical functions: it parses input sentences into structured representations and evaluates previously learned rules based on a subset of available training data. By continuously refining its expertise on these limited datasets, FPIO effectively balances its ability to interpret new input sentences accurately and adapt its internal ruleset to reflect the nuanced characteristics of these datasets. Experimental findings show that FPIO surpasses its direct competitors in evaluations utilizing smaller training sets and holds comparable performance to that of traditional parsers when larger numbers of training instances are involved, thus making it particularly suitable for scenarios where valuable annotated data is abundant.

In recent years, there has been significant growth in the use of semantic segmentation in various fields like computer vision and remote sensing. The traditional methods for annotation are time-consuming and expensive for images and instances of objects or targets are typically denoted with basic labels. Nevertheless, advancements in hyperspectral image technology enable automated and semi-automated refinement of class labels, resulting in precise pixel-level classification information. The main challenge lies in developing an effective learning method that can leverage this detailed classification information to learn robust representations suitable for tasks such as classification and detection. This paper presents a novel self-supervised method, Refine2Reco, for reconstructing spectral images from coarse labels using detailed classification information. Refine2Reco involves two interconnected modules, one for aligning spectral images with coarse labels and another for matching images with maps of spectral distributions. Comprehensive tests on two datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in preparing spectral images for coarse labels, resulting in improved performance for downstream tasks by approximately 3% compared to the current state-of-the-art techniques. The source code for our method can be found on our GitHub repository at https://github.com/Refine2Reco/Code.

The analysis of data from TESS Channels 1 and 2 revealed an anomaly in the rotation rate of the star KIC 9267654, which should be rotating every 7.15 days based before space missions, but which appears to have completed only 170.4 +/- 1.3 rotations in 817 days of TESS observation, instead of the 120 rotations expected. Various potential explanations for this unusual rotation pattern were explored: an oblique dipole magnetic field aligned with the star's north pole was found to be unlikely to be the cause due to lack of associated magnetic activity; a cool spot on the star's surface reflecting TESS's wide field of view and changing orientation due to the star's rotation was another possibility examined; and the presence of a disc or planet/comet dust cloud around the star was another explanation to be explored. Ultimately, all explanations were unsatisfactory and further observation is needed to solve this mystery.

This paper presents a modified RAM model for general-purpose computing, capable of handling arbitrary-precision integers. We define two integer types - positive and negative general-purpose integers, and establish the relationship between them, including how they can be used to represent any polynomial integer. To optimize memory usage, we introduce a shift register with a fixed width, capable of storing input/output and shifting it left or right by specified amounts. We analyze the efficiency of this model by demonstrating its ability to handle input/output of up to $k \log_2 c$ bits in $O(k + \log_2 c)$ steps for a polynomial integer $c$, with $k$ being the number of words. We also show that it can perform basic arithmetic operations in $O(\log_2 c)$ steps, such as addition and multiplication. Furthermore, we introduce two extensions to the model - a boolean word and a random number generator, and demonstrate their feasibility in $O(1)$ steps. Finally, we discuss the equivalence in computational power between our model and a Turing machine with the same word size and writing system.

Session-based recommendation is gaining more attention due to its broader applicability and easier data collection compared to other recommendation systems. It involves predicting the next interaction in a session by learning from historical interactions. However, its recommendation accuracy is limited by the size and quality of available session data, which often suffers from significant augmentation challenges due to its discrete and sparse nature. Traditional approaches to enhance session-based recommendation through data augmentation have focused primarily on increasing the length of sessions through insertions or duplications, often leading to the creation of artificial sessions that don't naturally occur. To address this challenge, this work proposes a new data augmentation method grounded in self-supervised learning principles, aiming to produce more authentic session expansion insertions. By training models to create expansions that can be accurately condensed, this method enables the creation of more realistic session expansions. Our proposed method, which can be integrated with existing session-based recommendation models, demonstrates its effectiveness through experimental results using the retail, Alibaba, and Geometro datasets, showcasing improvements in prediction accuracy when combined with other data augmentation methods, such as inserting low-frequency items or expanding session activities.

This research investigates subgroups within a group of a finite abelian group of order n, focusing on LCD codes within these subsets. By imposing specific requirements on group ring elements, we can determine the characteristics of such codes and derive two distinct types of side classes to identify self-dual groups or double circulant codes within the class of group rings. This approach encompasses code constructions from Zgr for certain abelian groups and also encompasses multivariate quadratic code construction as a special instance.

Infinitesimal cohomology of group schemes can be understood as a space of invariant forms. We establish a similar principle in the context of a Lie algebra, where we introduce a new way to represent invariant elements in the cohomology of its associated Lie group. This approach enables us to identify the stable cohomology of the general linear group, as well as compute the stable cohomology of isotropic spin and special isotropic spin groups, and split isotropic spin groups.

We've modified the standard full connection in a short-term memory unit of recurrent neural networks with an auxiliary bidirectional connection, connecting every object in a scene to every other object. We examined this network architecture in the context of object categorization using semantic segmentation masks as inputs, and the results show that auxiliary variables greatly improve performance. Furthermore, our findings reveal that networks with auxiliary variables learn meaningful semantic relationships between different objects, which can be quantified and visualized using a semantic relationship matrix and t-SNE projections. We also discovered a correlation between a network's performance and the complexity of its learned relationships, highlighting a clear advantage of auxiliary variables. We believe this innovative network architecture could yield valuable insights for future object categorization tasks and related studies.

The non-Hermitian skin effect or NHSE represents a significant and distinctive characteristic of non-Hermitian systems. It refers to the substantial localization of eigenstates near the boundary in open boundary conditions, which are not present in their Hermitian counterparts. While initial research concentrated on simpler systems like the non-Hermitian tight-binding model, it has since expanded to include systems influenced by non-Hermitian couplings. Despite this, most examples remain within the class of non-Hermitian tight-binding models. The current work delves into the novel occurrence of the NHSE in a chain that incorporates non-Hermitian intra-site couplings, and explores its diverse manifestations beyond the conventional tight-Hopping Hopping model. Specifically, this study considers a non-Hermitian chain and examines the novel skin effect's occurrence despite the chain having no non-Hermitian inter-site coupling. Furthermore, this work investigates the novel skin effect's occurrence in chains conforming to chiral and antichiral symmetries, even when the chain's edge states remain precursors within the bulk and are influenced by balancing relationships with the adjoint system.

A quaternary Golay complementary array pair (GCAP) allows for the precise measurement of range and Doppler and is essential for designing efficient radar systems. Recently, closed-form formulas for GCAPs were developed based on mathematical structures known as difference sets and complementary quadruple quadruplets. This research expands GCAP availability by deriving different types of quadruplet-based quadruplet GCAPs, including generalized forms. Notably, it's discovered that GCAP feasibility is limited to specific lengths that meet particular mathematical criteria, such as being divisible by four or having particular remainder remainders when divided by 12. This research also presents quadruplet GCAP construction methods that could potentially benefit array signal processing.

Recent LHC Run 2 data from the ATLAS and CMS experiments have placed new constraints on the Higgs boson's unusual interactions with vector bosons in accordance with the Standard Model Higgs model. By the end of 2018, the LHC has been/lhas accumulated a total of 13 TeV center-of-mass proton-proton collision data. LHC experiments then compared the observed one-, two-, and three-vector boson final states and found that they're in line with standard model predictions, with a 1-5% deviation from the standard model, and the 95% confidence level. LHC experiments then performed the most comprehensive search to date, combining final states to form the most stringent constraints to date, and found that the constraints on anomalous Higgs boson vector boson couplings are as follows: $|V_{1}|\lt 0.004$, $|V_{2}|\lt 0.002$, and $|V_{3}|\lt 0.001$, and the constraints on the related parameters are as follows: the expectations for the standard model.

Change detection in multi-temporal satellite images without prior labels is more suitable for various applications, as it doesn't require heavily annotated data.  However, unlabeled data presents a challenge since there's no ground truth for potential missed changes or false alarms.  To address this issue, we propose an innovative deep learning framework that utilizes a self-supervised approach to learn a representation for detecting changes in building images.  Our framework integrates a self-supervised learning (SSL) module with a change detection model to enhance its generalization ability on unseen data.  Furthermore, we introduce a multi-task learning module that simultaneously performs changedetection and representation learning to improve detection accuracy.  Our extensive experiments on numerous datasets reveal that our framework achieves remarkable results, surpassing current state-of-the-art methods by a substantial margin.  Notably, the model's performance on novel data types discovered during testing is comparable to that trained on thoroughly labeled datasets, demonstrating its exceptional ability to generalize on entirely new data types.

Building upon the work of Nathanson and Shen, we refine their findings by proving that for any base $a \geq 3$, the asymptotic behavior of the representing function $I_{\square + A}(n)$ is given by $c \cdot n - O_n(\log n)$, where the error term has been significantly reduced. Previously, Lu proved an error term of $O_n(\sqrt{n})$, while we achieve a error term of $O_n(\log n)$, a major improvement upon the original result of $O_n(\sqrt{n})$.

Precise control of Heisenberg spin exchange interaction is vital for producing high-fidelity two-qubit gates for quantum processors based on silicon-28. By manipulating valence bond formation in a silicon lattice through dopant placement, the position of isotopes that interact via the hyperfine interaction can be controlled, thus adjusting the coupling strength between spins. A gradient in valence bond bondlength is demonstrated using a few silicon atoms and one carbon dopant within a silicon lattice, with a measurement precision of 0.042 Angstrom. This level of control provides a level of precision comparable to that required for quantum computing with spins.

This paper outlines the IBRA framework, a comprehensive Python library designed for population-based direct search algorithms, which is employed to solve direct optimization problems. The framework is not limited to solving these problems, but also serves as a teaching tool and a means for researchers to develop, examine, and compare various algorithms, as well as populate-based indirect search methods. Comprising four modules - Core, Educator, Explorer, and Exploiter - IBRA facilitates the rapid development and comparison of diverse algorithms through predefined functions. Exploiter module contains numerous benchmarking functions, while Explorer and Explorer_ext modules comprise a vast collection of benchmarking functions, totaling 130. A vast collection of benchmarking functions, totaling 130, is provided, with Exploiter module containing numerous functions, while Explorer and Explorer_ext modules comprising a vast collection of benchmarking functions, totaling 130.

We have calculated the transitivity degree for complete linearized logarithmic forms of weights and for the algebra of invariant polynomials of multilogarithms on algebraic varieties of logarithmic type, which are known to be finitely generated. We have discovered a distinct expression for the transitivity degree formula in this context, and demonstrated distinct module generator bases of logarithmic forms and multilogarithmic forms on these varieties.

We have developed formalisms for key attributes of multi-particle methods in non-abelian quantum mechanics, including the total momentum, Hamiltonian eigenstates and eigenvalues, and the eigenstates of individual particle momenta. The framework also considers the projection of the total wave function onto individual particle states and the resulting non-abelian scattering matrix. Our framework is applicable to multi-particle bound states and is demonstrated through 3D harmonic oscillator bound state calculations, showing both exact and approximate results for vibrational spectra.

To analyze the two-photon absorption of light in a semiconductor, we examine the direct transition between the valence and conduction bands by introducing an external electric field $F$ along specific crystallographic axes. Due to the inherent complexities of selecting appropriate wave functions at the Gamma point without detailed knowledge of the band structure, we employ a general approach, representing the relevant valence and conduction band wave functions using known angular momentum eigenstates. By applying this external field, which induces a perturbation in the Hamiltonian, we demonstrate that it is primarily the two-photon absorption process involving one field photon and one external field photon that contributes to the generation of free charge carriers through the direct valence-to-conduction band transition. By evaluating the perturbed wave functions at the Gamma point, which describe both valence and conduction bands, we obtain the matrix element governing the two-photon absorption process. By applying the Fermi-Golden rule and performing the integration over all photon directions and polarizations, which plays a crucial role in understanding the phenomenon, we derive the rate of free charge carrier generation due to two-photon absorption process. By relating the absorption coefficient to the free charge carrier generation rate, which provides governing insight, we obtain valuable insights into the behavior of free charge carriers under two-photon absorption processes in semiconductors.

Misogynistic language is a global concern that demands an effective response.
As the internet produces vast amounts of textual data, it has become crucial to
have a reliable method for detecting and monitoring such content. This research
proposes MisogyniGPT, a framework that leverages a LLM to identify and flag
misogynistic expressions in both English and Spanish texts. By fine-tuning a
pre-trained LLM, specifically MARBERT, on a customized dataset containing
examples of misogyny, a high level of accuracy in classification is achieved.
MisogyniGPT's performance excels compared to existing models, with a significant
improvement in F1 score of 37.1% over TUM Rule-Misogynist.

This research focuses on a form of backward stochastic differential equation, where its generator has access to the equation's solution's historical values, thereby leading to a rough path type backward equation. Unlike previous approaches, which involved predicting future values through a "memorizer network," we develop a adaptive stepsize method based on a pathwise Lipschitz condition, eliminating the need for such predictions. Consequently, this condition enables us to establish unique existence results, first proving well-posedness for a rough path equation, and then for the original backward differential equation with subsequent convergence results.

Reinforcement learning achieves exceptional performance in control systems, albeit through an extremely difficult process. Robotic controllers, whose safety is crucial, cannot be reliably obtained via typical reinforcement learning methods, partly because the learning distributions are non-stationary and partly because the learning processes are highly sensitive to minor disturbances. We propose an strategy for learning distributions, which, when incorporated into the dynamics model, enhances the robustness of the resulting controller. This is done by introducing a minimum threshold for noise level in the dynamics model, the parameters of which are refined through amortized training. Subsequent controller learning, which is done off-policy, yields robust controllers, which are also more consistent and reliable. We observed enhanced robustness, reduced variance and improved safety on stochastic Monte-Carlo simulations of a difficult balancing task.

A proposed method for coded caching creates a link between the design of caching schemes and combinatorial objectives, projecting existing codelibraries onto users' caches in two stages.  The method divides the library in two stages, applying (1) a standard linear splitting strategy and (2) a cooperative partitioning strategy that links users' caches to combinations of files.  It is demonstrated that popular integer programming formulations can achieve optimal results when applied to this two-stage process, and it is shown that several popular schemes are simply result of applying well-known codelibraries in a two-stage process, including cooperative subpacketizing and index range schemes.  The framework also provides a way to analyze the performance of these popular schemes.  It is further demonstrated that the capacity of the cooperative subpacketizing scheme can be calculated through a projection of the linear code used, while the optimal performance of the index range scheme can be determined through a projection of a Z4-lattice into a lower-dimensional space.  This method also provides a projection that matches the optimal sum-rate of the index range scheme with the cross-subpacketizing scheme.  A two-stage framework is presented in which the code is applied to combinations of files, while projection occurs in two steps, resulting in a framework where the code is applied in two stages and projection occurs as users retrieve files.  It is shown that the cross-subpacketizing scheme can be optimally designed through this method, while the capacity of the index range scheme can be calculated through

This study explores the Scott model in detail to understand its value in studying programming languages within a predicative and constructive setting.  We examine how elements in this model can be used to develop an interactive meta-logic for reasoning about programs with multiple levels of abstraction, specifically those with simultaneous existence and constructive overlap.  Using the Scott model, we create a predicative version of Scott-Set Existential Quantification (SCSQ) and develop an interactive framework for studying languages with higher-order simultaneous recurrence.  Within this framework, we develop interactive forms of induction and mutual recursion principles, using the Scott model to prove their correctness through a process of double interpretation.

A detailed examination of specific degenerate Eisenstein series for Sp(3,Z) is provided in this paper. We explicitly express their non-constant terms using an integral of a Weyl group-related function on the positive Weyl group manifolds. This function exhibits exceptional properties of being both harmonic and eigenfunction, belonging to the representation 79 of (SL(3,C), U(q(3))) and possessing a particular eigenvalue.

Our key contribution lies in integrating the spatial arrangement of a mobile robotic arm into model predictive control (MPC) for collision avoidance. Building on our previous work, we modeled the arm's space using Voronoi diagrams, partitioning it into distinct areas. Each area is associated with a Markov decision process (MDP), representing both safe states and collisions. State-transitions occur not only based on the robot's movements but also due to obstacles' changes. This approach considers various scenarios, such as mobile obstacles stopping suddenly or the robot missing its target. Our results demonstrate that this method effectively balances task completion and collision avoidance, making it a valuable framework for real-world applications.

To effectively process and connect with people, NLP must successfully navigate the gap between various forms of written and spoken communication and the underlying meanings they convey. The most crucial tasks in NLP involve understanding and generating speech, understanding and generating text, extracting relevant information from documents, and understanding the structure and semantics of sentences. Although tremendous progress has been made in addressing these challenges, particularly with the development of large-scale transformer models and self-supervised learning, significant issues remain to be resolved, such as comprehension of complex language structures and figures of speech, understanding the sounds of language, and mastering the intricacies of written and spoken communication.

The sensitivity of Ramsey interferometry to phase shifts experienced by a Bose-Einstein condensate can be improved by using Hadamard gates that introduce nonlinear phase shifts. This results in a peak in the Ramsey interferometry signal that non-parametrically captures environmental phase information, making it applicable to various scenarios. Additionally, the use of multiple nonlinear interferometers, tuned to distinct sensitivities, allows for optimal estimation of environmental phase shifts by adapting Ramsey imaging to match the uncertainty principle at working points.

This paper deals with several new value distribution theories for non-linear mappings between complex spaces. Specifically, it establishes several Novel Value Sharing Theorems that consider how meromorphic mappings interact with given subsets, including hypersurfaces and hyperplanes in complex projective spaces, while also sharing the same values. These findings generalize and extend notable works of Ru, Griffor, Liu, and Grifor from their original formulations. Ultimately, this study aims to provide unique sharing results for value distribution theories within complex multi-dimensional spaces.

This paper presents an innovative approach that adapts signature-based Gröbner basis algorithms for efficient computation of Gröbner basis descriptions of multihomogeneous ideal bases. By adding a finite relationship between variables and bounding the degrees of the Gröbner basis algorithm, we improve upon existing Reuttenauer's method. Furthermore, we develop hybrid strategies combining Groebner basis and resultant based approaches to solve multihomogeneous systems. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms Gröbner basis algorithms using total ordering in various applications.

The collaboration with the STAR Collaboration involved analyzing startrackers for a comprehensive review of background particle photons in heavy ion collisions. Our focus was on data from 200 GeV Cu+Cu and Au+Au collisions, where the detector's field of view allowed for a detailed study of the particle shower geometry. In Cu+Cu collisions, we found that photonrapidity density was 70% lower than that of charged particles, while in Au+Au collisions, the photon and charged particle densities were comparable. We observed a significant rise in photon-to-charged particle ratios at the edge of the detector in both datasets, suggesting an increased presence of photons near the collision zone.

A co-2-normally 4-colorable 2-uniform 4-clique-free hypergraph is defined as one whose vertices can partition into four sets such that any sub-hypergraph formed by these sets has at most one edge. The function exco_2(n,H) represents the maximum number of edges in such a hypergraph on n vertices. We establish the limits of exco_2(n,H) under certain conditions, specifically when H is isomorphic or 4-partite as opposed to not 4-partite, yielding distinct upper bounds. When H is not 4-partite, we show exco_2(n,H) has a maximum limit of O(n^(3/2)). When H is 4-partite, we show exco_2(n,H) has a maximum limit of O(n). Furthermore, we demonstrate this limit of O(n) is attainable under certain conditions, particularly when H contains a 4-partite cycle of 8 vertices. A related theorem is also stated, proposing a bound of exco_2(n,H) as O(n) when H satisfies additional colorability conditions.

Rendering geometric shapes like polygons and circles with line joins often relies on approximating fan shapes using triangles. This method has a significant drawback of producing unsightly artifacts at the junction where two triangles meet. In response to this issue, we have developed an algorithm that utilizes strip topology to triangle fans, enabling smoother rendering of these graphics. Although this approach increases rendering complexity, careful analysis shows that rendering performance using GPU hardware remains comparable to the traditional method. Although GPU triangles can technically be rendered slightly faster than fan-shaped graphics due to their reliance on a single index buffer, our research has demonstrated that the difference in performance is negligible. This makes the proposed technique an attractive option for enhancing line join rendering performance.

This study develops a quasi-interpolation formula based on the exponential RBF $e^{cx}$ with $c > 0$. Unlike traditional methods, our approach maintains convexity and monotonicity while providing a precise function value at specified points. A key application considered is the numerical solution of the fractional Caputo derivative problem. We approximate the fractional derivative using difference formulas and transform the difference operator into a pseudopointwise matrix via the derived quasi-interpolation formula. With help from M-wellposedness theory, we establish the convergence order of the resulting numerical method. Further analysis includes properties of the fractional Laplace operator's symbol and the matrix generated by our difference operator, which helps us derive lower bounds and study convergence. Moreover, we demonstrate the numerical method's stability and obtain solutions with the help of an iterative method, studying its convergence. Two examples are provided to demonstrate the accuracy and validity of our approach.
